title: Mountain Pose
desc: The reference standing shape. Feet rooted, crown lifting, arms at the sides — every other standing asana is measured against the alignment learned here.

title: Upward Salute
desc: Tadasana with the arms sweeping overhead. Opens the front body and sets the first inhale of a sun salutation.

title: Standing Forward Fold
desc: A full forward hinge from the hips with the spine long. Calms the nervous system and lengthens the whole posterior chain.

title: Half Forward Fold
desc: The flat-back halfway lift between fold and step back. Teaches spinal length before the hamstrings are asked to release.

title: Four-Limbed Staff Pose
desc: A low push-up hold with elbows tracking back over the wrists. The most commonly rushed shape in vinyasa and the most common source of shoulder strain.

title: Upward-Facing Dog
desc: Thighs lifted clear of the floor, chest drawing forward through the arms. A true backbend rather than a rest, unlike cobra.

title: Cobra Pose
desc: A low chest lift with the legs and pelvis grounded and very little arm push. The gentler backbend of the sun salutation family.

title: Downward-Facing Dog
desc: An inverted V with hips lifting and heels descending. The most-used shape in modern practice and a mild inversion in its own right.

title: Plank Pose
desc: A straight line from crown to heels supported on hands and toes. Builds the shoulder and core stability every arm balance later depends on.

title: Knees-Chest-Chin
desc: Eight points touching the floor — knees, chest and chin — as the gentler alternative to chaturanga in classical sun salutations.

title: Low Lunge
desc: Back knee down, hips sinking forward, arms often overhead. The primary hip flexor opener and a staple of the sun salutation cycle.

title: High Lunge
desc: Back heel lifted, front knee stacked over the ankle, torso upright. Strong in the legs and demanding on balance in a way low lunge is not.

title: Staff Pose
desc: Seated with legs extended and spine vertical. The seated counterpart to tadasana and the reference for every seated forward bend.

title: Warrior I
desc: Front knee bent, back foot angled in, hips and chest turning forward with arms overhead. Squares the pelvis in a way the other warriors do not.

title: Warrior II
desc: Hips open to the side, arms extended front and back, gaze over the front hand. Builds the leg endurance the standing sequence is named for.

title: Reverse Warrior
desc: Warrior II with the front arm sweeping overhead and the torso arching back. A side-body opener rather than a true backbend.

title: Extended Side Angle
desc: Front forearm on thigh or hand to floor, top arm reaching over the ear in one long diagonal from back heel to fingertips.

title: Triangle Pose
desc: Legs straight and wide, torso hinging sideways over the front leg. Lengthens the side body while the hamstrings work eccentrically.

title: Revolved Triangle
desc: Triangle with the torso rotated so the opposite hand reaches the floor. Balance and hamstring length are both tested at once.

title: Wide-Legged Forward Fold
desc: Feet wide and parallel, torso folding between them with the crown descending. A gentle inversion and a strong inner-thigh stretch.

title: Pyramid Pose
desc: Hips squared over a short stance, torso folding along a straight front leg. More intense on the hamstrings than uttanasana because the pelvis cannot rotate away.

title: Chair Pose
desc: Knees bent deep with weight in the heels and arms lifting overhead. Heats the body quickly and is the classic kapha-reducing standing shape.

title: Revolved Chair
desc: Chair pose with the torso rotated and the opposite elbow outside the knee. Combines leg endurance with a closed twist.

title: Standing Half Forward Bend at Wall
desc: Hands on a wall, torso folding to horizontal with a long spine. The accessible entry to downward dog for stiff shoulders or hamstrings.

title: Garland Pose
desc: A deep squat with heels down and elbows pressing the knees wide. The everyday resting squat of much of the world, and a strong hip opener for those who have lost it.

title: Standing Wide Squat
desc: A wide-footed squat with the torso upright, less demanding on ankle range than malasana and better tolerated by stiff hips.

title: Goddess Pose
desc: Feet wide and turned out, knees bent to a wide squat, arms in cactus. Builds heat fast and opens the hips at the same time.

title: Standing Side Bend
desc: Feet together, arms overhead, torso curving to one side. The simplest way to open the intercostals and lengthen the side waist.

title: Warrior III
desc: A single-leg balance with torso and lifted leg forming one horizontal line. Demands hamstring strength and proprioception together.

title: Tree Pose
desc: One foot rooted, the other sole pressed to the inner calf or thigh. The first balance most practitioners learn and a lifelong measure of steadiness.

title: Eagle Pose
desc: Arms and legs each double-wrapped while the hips sink. Compresses and then floods the joints, and demands focus to hold.

title: Dancer Pose
desc: Standing on one leg while the other is caught behind and lifted into a backbend. Balance, backbend and shoulder opening at once.

title: Half Moon Pose
desc: Balanced on one leg and one hand with the top leg and arm reaching apart. Opens the hip while testing lateral stability.

title: Revolved Half Moon
desc: Half moon with the torso rotated toward the standing leg. One of the harder standing balances because the twist removes the visual reference.

title: Extended Hand-to-Big-Toe
desc: Standing on one leg with the other extended and held at the toe. Exposes any hamstring shortness immediately.

title: Standing Split
desc: A forward fold on one leg with the other lifting toward vertical. Hamstring length and balance combined, often approached from half moon.

title: Warrior I Twist
desc: Warrior I with the torso rotating over the front thigh. Strong legs beneath a closed twist, and hard on the sacroiliac joint if forced.

title: Humble Warrior
desc: Warrior I with fingers interlaced behind the back and the torso folding inside the front leg. A shoulder opener disguised as a standing pose.

title: Crescent Lunge Twist
desc: High lunge with the torso rotated and the opposite elbow to the outer knee. A common vinyasa transition and a genuine detoxifying twist.

title: Gate Pose
desc: Kneeling on one leg with the other extended sideways and the torso bending over it. Opens the side body without loading the hamstrings.

title: Standing Backbend
desc: An upright backbend with hands supporting the sacrum. Often the closing shape of a sun salutation's first inhale.

title: Five-Pointed Star
desc: Feet wide, arms wide, body forming a five-pointed star. Used as a transition and a chest opener between wider standing shapes.

title: Wide-Legged Forward Fold with Clasp
desc: The wide fold with fingers interlaced behind the back and arms descending overhead. Adds a strong shoulder opening to the hamstring stretch.

title: Intense Side Stretch with Reverse Prayer
desc: Pyramid pose with the palms pressed together behind the back. Demands more wrist and shoulder range than the fold itself.

title: Chair Pose with Prayer Twist
desc: Revolved chair with palms in prayer and the lower elbow hooked outside the opposite knee. The deepest of the standing twists.

title: Warrior II Side Bend
desc: Side angle with the bottom hand reaching to the floor outside the front foot rather than resting on the thigh.

title: Bound Angle Pose
desc: Seated with soles together and knees dropping wide. The primary seated hip opener and a common preparation for meditation seats.

title: Reclined Bound Angle
desc: Bound angle taken lying down, usually over a bolster. One of the most reliably calming shapes in the whole restorative repertoire.

title: Head-to-Knee Pose
desc: One leg extended and one folded in, torso folding over the straight leg. Asymmetry lets a tight side be worked without the other compensating.

title: Seated Forward Bend
desc: Both legs extended, torso folding forward over them. The archetypal forward bend and the one most often forced from the low back instead of the hips.

title: Revolved Head-to-Knee
desc: A seated side bend and twist over one straight leg with the top arm reaching overhead. Opens the side body more than the hamstrings.

title: Wide-Angle Seated Forward Bend
desc: Legs wide and straight, torso folding forward between them. A demanding adductor stretch that rewards patience over depth.

title: Cow Face Pose
desc: Knees stacked and arms clasped behind the back in opposite directions. Simultaneously one of the hardest hip and shoulder openers.

title: Hero Pose
desc: Kneeling with the hips settling between the heels. A classical meditation seat that opens the quadriceps and ankles over time.

title: Reclined Hero
desc: Hero pose reclined backward onto elbows or the floor. A profound quadriceps and hip flexor opener that must never be forced at the knee.

title: Thunderbolt Pose
desc: Kneeling with the buttocks on the heels. Traditionally the one asana said to be safe immediately after eating, which is why it carries its digestive reputation.

title: Easy Pose
desc: A simple cross-legged seat with the spine upright. The default meditation posture when lotus is unavailable, which for most adults it is.

title: Half Lotus
desc: One foot drawn onto the opposite thigh, the other tucked beneath. The usual stepping stone toward full lotus and a stable seat in its own right.

title: Lotus Pose
desc: Both feet drawn onto the opposite thighs. The classical seat of the texts, and one that must come from external hip rotation rather than knee torque.

title: Accomplished Pose
desc: A cross-legged seat with one heel at the perineum, named for the adepts. Favoured in the hatha texts over lotus for long pranayama sessions.

title: Seated Twist
desc: The half lord of the fishes — one knee upright, torso rotating toward it. The reference seated twist of modern practice.

title: Full Lord of the Fishes
desc: The bound full expression of the seated twist with the arms wrapping the leg. Requires shoulder range as much as spinal rotation.

title: Sage Marichi I
desc: A bound forward fold with one knee upright and the arms clasping around it. Named for the sage Marichi, one of a family of four.

title: Sage Marichi III
desc: A bound seated twist with the arm hooked outside the upright knee. The bind deepens the rotation well beyond the unbound version.

title: Boat Pose
desc: Balanced on the sitting bones with legs and torso lifted into a V. The primary seated core shape and a reliable heat builder.

title: Half Boat Pose
desc: Boat pose with the knees bent and shins parallel to the floor. The accessible version, and the honest one for most beginners.

title: Seated Wide-Legged Twist
desc: A wide-legged seated position with the torso rotating and folding over one leg. Combines adductor stretch with rotation.

title: Firelog Pose
desc: Shins stacked one directly above the other. One of the most intense external hip rotations available seated, and unforgiving of knee compensation.

title: Half Pigeon
desc: Front shin angled across the mat, back leg extending straight behind. The most widely taught hip opener in modern classes.

title: King Pigeon
desc: Pigeon with the back foot caught overhead and the spine arching. A deep backbend that needs the hip flexors open first.

title: Double Pigeon
desc: Shins crossed and stacked with the torso folding forward. A gentler entry to the firelog shape for tighter hips.

title: Lizard Pose
desc: A deep lunge with both hands inside the front foot and forearms often lowering. Opens the hip in flexion and the groin at once.

title: Frog Pose
desc: Knees wide and shins out with the hips sinking toward the floor. A very strong adductor opener that must be entered slowly.

title: Butterfly Fold
desc: Bound angle with the torso folding forward over the feet. Lengthens the low back while the adductors release.

title: Compass Pose
desc: One leg lifted over the shoulder and extended straight while the torso rotates. Among the most demanding seated shapes for hamstring and shoulder range together.

title: Heron Pose
desc: One leg folded in hero position, the other lifted straight toward the face. A seated hamstring stretch with no floor to lean on.

title: Tortoise Pose
desc: A deep wide-legged fold with the arms threading beneath the knees. Named for the withdrawal of the senses it is said to produce.

title: Sleeping Tortoise
desc: Tortoise with the ankles crossed behind the head and the hands bound. One of the deepest folds in the Ashtanga primary series.

title: Bharadvaja's Twist
desc: A gentle seated twist with both legs folded to one side. The most accessible of the named seated twists and safe for most backs.

title: Sage Vasistha's Pose
desc: A side plank on one hand with the body in a single line. Builds lateral core strength that plank alone does not reach.

title: Side Plank with Leg Lift
desc: Side plank with the top leg lifted or caught at the toe. Adds hamstring length and a balance demand to the side hold.

title: Staff Pose Lift
desc: Lifting the whole crossed-legged body clear of the floor on the hands. The closing lift of the Ashtanga series and a pure test of core and shoulder strength.

title: Seated Cat-Cow
desc: Spinal flexion and extension performed sitting. The version that works for chairs, for pregnancy and for anyone who cannot kneel.

title: Seated Side Stretch
desc: A cross-legged seat with one arm reaching overhead and the torso curving sideways. The gentlest side-body opener in the catalogue.

title: Cradle Stretch
desc: One shin cradled in the arms and rocked side to side. Opens the outer hip without loading the knee the way pigeon can.

title: Seated Forward Bend with Strap
desc: The seated fold with a strap around the feet so the spine can stay long. The honest version for tight hamstrings and the one that actually progresses.

title: Half Bound Lotus Forward Bend
desc: Half lotus with the foot bound behind the back and the torso folding over the straight leg. Knee, hip and shoulder range all required at once.

title: Bridge Pose
desc: Feet planted and hips lifting with the shoulders rolled beneath. The entry backbend and a safe preparation for wheel.

title: Supported Bridge
desc: Bridge with a block under the sacrum so the shape is held without effort. A passive chest opener and a mild inversion.

title: Wheel Pose
desc: A full backbend pressing up from hands and feet. The most heating shape in the catalogue and the one most often attempted before the shoulders are ready.

title: Camel Pose
desc: Kneeling and arching back with hands reaching for the heels. Opens the whole front body and is famously destabilising emotionally.

title: Bow Pose
desc: Lying prone, ankles caught in the hands, chest and thighs lifting into a bow. Strong compression of the low back and full opening of the front.

title: Locust Pose
desc: Prone with the chest, arms and legs lifting away from the floor. The best strengthener for the posterior chain in the whole repertoire.

title: Half Locust
desc: Locust with one leg lifting at a time. Halves the load and lets a weaker side be trained honestly.

title: Sphinx Pose
desc: A gentle prone backbend supported on the forearms. Sustained and passive rather than muscular, and well tolerated by most low backs.

title: Seal Pose
desc: The yin version of a prone backbend with straight arms and a long hold. Deep compression of the lumbar spine over minutes rather than seconds.

title: Fish Pose
desc: Reclined with the chest lifting and the crown resting lightly on the floor. The classical counterpose to shoulderstand.

title: Supported Fish
desc: Fish taken over a bolster so the chest opens without any muscular effort. One of the best shapes for a desk-bound upper back.

title: Upward Bow with Blocks
desc: Wheel with the hands elevated on blocks against a wall. Reduces the shoulder range required and is the right way in for most people.

title: Little Thunderbolt
desc: Kneeling and arching back until the crown touches the floor with the thighs still working. A controlled descent that demands quadriceps strength.

title: Pigeon King Prep with Strap
desc: Pigeon with a strap looped around the back foot so the bind can be approached gradually.

title: Cat Pose
desc: On hands and knees with the spine rounding toward the ceiling. Half of the most-taught spinal warm-up in yoga.

title: Cow Pose
desc: On hands and knees with the belly dropping and the chest lifting. The other half of cat-cow, and the gentlest backbend available.

title: Thread the Needle
desc: From all fours, one arm threading beneath the body to the opposite side. Releases the upper back and rear shoulder with no strain.

title: Puppy Pose
desc: Hips over knees with the chest melting toward the floor and arms extended. A shoulder opener without the load of downward dog.

title: Child's Pose
desc: Kneeling and folding forward with the forehead down. The universal resting shape and the one to return to whenever a practice becomes too much.

title: Wide-Knee Child's Pose
desc: Child's pose with the knees wide so the belly can settle between the thighs. Better tolerated in pregnancy and by larger bodies.

title: Extended Puppy with Blocks
desc: Puppy pose supported on blocks so the heart opening can be held for minutes. Named for the heart centre it is said to work on.

title: Knees-to-Chest
desc: Lying on the back with both knees hugged in. Named for apana vayu, the downward-moving breath, and used to settle the low back and the gut.

title: Supine Twist
desc: Knees dropping to one side while the shoulders stay grounded. The gentlest twist available and the standard closing shape before savasana.

title: Reclined Hand-to-Big-Toe
desc: Lying on the back with one leg extended upward and held by a strap or the toe. The safest place to work on hamstring length.

title: Reclined Pigeon
desc: Ankle crossed over the opposite thigh with the legs drawn in. The figure-four shape, and the accessible version of pigeon for stiff or injured hips.

title: Happy Baby
desc: On the back with knees drawn wide toward the armpits and feet held. Opens the hips while the low back stays flat and safe.

title: Legs Up the Wall
desc: Lying with the legs vertical against a wall. A mild inversion with most of the benefit and almost none of the risk of shoulderstand.

title: Corpse Pose
desc: Lying completely still on the back. The hardest asana to do properly and the one the whole practice is arranged to make possible.

title: Reclined Twist with Bolster
desc: A supine twist with the knees resting on a bolster so nothing has to be held. Suitable for long holds and for pregnancy.

title: Wind-Relieving Pose
desc: One knee drawn firmly into the chest while the other leg stays long. Named directly for its effect on trapped digestive gas.

title: Supine Bound Angle with Strap
desc: Reclined bound angle with a strap holding the legs so no muscular effort is needed. The standard long-hold restorative hip shape.

title: Constructive Rest
desc: Lying with knees bent and feet planted so the low back can release. The alternative to savasana for anyone whose back complains lying flat.

title: Shoulderstand
desc: Body vertical on the shoulders with the neck supported. Called the queen of asanas in the classical literature, and genuinely risky for the cervical spine when unsupported.

title: Halasana Plough
desc: From shoulderstand, the feet lowering to the floor behind the head. Very strong on the cervical spine and never to be entered by dropping.

title: Ear Pressure Pose
desc: Plough with the knees folding beside the ears. Deeper spinal flexion still, and only appropriate once plough is entirely comfortable.

title: Headstand
desc: Balanced on the forearms and crown with the body vertical. The king of asanas classically, and the shape with the highest injury cost when learned without supervision.

title: Supported Headstand at Wall
desc: Headstand practised with the wall behind so the legs cannot swing past vertical. The honest way to learn the shape.

title: Forearm Stand
desc: A full inversion balanced on the forearms. Demands more shoulder flexion than handstand and is often easier to hold once entered.

title: Handstand
desc: A full inversion on the hands. The most athletically demanding shape in the catalogue and the one that most rewards patient wall work.

title: Dolphin Pose
desc: Downward dog on the forearms. The single best preparation for forearm stand and a strong shoulder builder in its own right.

title: Crow Pose
desc: Knees resting on the upper arms with the feet lifting. The first arm balance most practitioners achieve, and more about weight shift than strength.

title: Crane Pose
desc: Crow with the arms straight and the knees high in the armpits. Considerably harder than bent-arm crow and often confused with it.

title: Side Crow
desc: A twisted arm balance with both knees resting on one upper arm. Rotation and balance combined, and a common gateway to the harder balances.

title: Eight-Angle Pose
desc: Legs threaded around one arm and extended sideways while the elbows bend. Named for the sage born with eight bends in his body.

title: Firefly Pose
desc: Seated on the hands with both legs extending forward and up. Requires open hamstrings as much as arm strength.

title: Flying Pigeon
desc: One shin hooked across the upper arms with the other leg extending straight back. A hip opener and an arm balance at the same time.

title: Peacock Pose
desc: Balanced horizontally on the elbows pressed into the belly. Classically said to digest even the most difficult food, and brutal on the wrists.

title: Scale Pose
desc: Lifting the whole lotus-seated body clear of the floor. A pure strength lift with no momentum available.

title: Rooster Pose
desc: Arms threaded through a lotus and the body lifted. Demands full lotus before the balance can even be attempted.

title: Shoulder-Pressing Pose
desc: Legs hooked over the shoulders with the feet crossed in front. A compact, compressed arm balance from the Ashtanga primary series.

title: Grasshopper Pose
desc: A deeply twisted arm balance with one foot hooked over the opposite arm. One of the more advanced rotational balances.

title: Crow to Headstand Transition
desc: Lowering from crow into tripod headstand and back. A controlled strength transition, not a drop.

title: Tripod Headstand
desc: A headstand with the hands forward forming a tripod. The entry point for many arm balance transitions.

title: Chin Stand
desc: Chest and chin on the floor with the legs arching overhead. Among the most extreme shapes in the catalogue and rarely appropriate.

title: Boat to Low Boat
desc: Alternating between full boat and a low hover just off the floor. The standard core conditioning cycle of the Ashtanga series.

title: Forearm Plank
desc: Plank supported on the forearms rather than the hands. Removes the wrist load and is often the better hold for beginners.

title: Side Plank Knee Down
desc: Side plank with the lower knee grounded. The accessible version and the right place to build lateral strength.

title: Dolphin Plank
desc: A forearm plank with the shoulders stacked over the elbows. The single best strengthener for forearm stand preparation.

title: Knee-to-Nose
desc: From downward dog, one knee drawing toward the nose with the spine rounding. A common vinyasa transition and a genuine core contraction.

title: Three-Legged Dog
desc: Downward dog with one leg lifting behind. The standard preparation for stepping through to a lunge.

title: Wild Thing
desc: From side plank, the top leg stepping back as the chest opens into a backbend. Modern in origin and enthusiastically taught in flow classes.

title: Downward Dog Split Twist
desc: Three-legged dog with the hip opening and the knee bending. Opens the outer hip but stresses the sacroiliac joint if the shoulders collapse.

title: Chaturanga to Upward Dog
desc: The linking movement of every vinyasa. Repeated dozens of times a class, which is exactly why its alignment matters more than any single pose.

title: Jump Back
desc: Lifting from a seated position and floating back to chaturanga. A strength skill that takes years, not a warm-up movement.

title: Jump Through
desc: Floating the legs through the arms from downward dog to seated. The counterpart to the jump back and equally demanding.

title: Handstand Hops
desc: Small hops toward vertical from a downward dog base. The safe way to find the balance point before committing to the full inversion.

title: Reverse Plank
desc: Hips lifting from a seated position with the body in a straight line facing up. The counterpose to the seated forward bend.

title: Upward Plank with Bent Knees
desc: Reverse plank with the knees bent and feet flat — the tabletop shape. Much kinder on the shoulders and hamstrings.

title: Downward Dog at Wall
desc: Hands on a wall at hip height with the torso horizontal. Teaches the shoulder action of downward dog without the weight.

title: Chair Twist at Chair
desc: A seated spinal twist performed in a chair. The accessible version for offices, older practitioners and limited mobility.

title: Standing Cat-Cow
desc: Spinal flexion and extension standing with hands on the thighs. Warms the spine when the floor is unavailable.

title: Wall Plank
desc: Plank performed against a wall. The entry point for building core and shoulder stability with almost no load.

title: Bird Dog
desc: From all fours, opposite arm and leg extending. Trains the cross-body stability that protects the low back in every standing pose.

title: Tabletop
desc: The neutral hands-and-knees position. The reference shape for cat-cow, bird dog and every kneeling transition.

title: Kneeling Side Plank
desc: A side plank from the knees with the top arm reaching up. Builds the oblique strength that full side plank later requires.

title: Hollow Body Hold
desc: Lying with shoulders and legs lifted and the low back pressed down. Borrowed from gymnastics and the most honest test of true core control.

title: Leg Lowering
desc: Legs lowering slowly from vertical toward the floor with the back flat. From the Ashtanga primary series and unforgiving of a lifting lumbar spine.

title: Supine Bicycle
desc: Alternating elbow to opposite knee on the back. Simple oblique conditioning used as a warm-up in many modern classes.

title: Three-Part Breath
desc: Filling the belly, then the ribs, then the upper chest in one long inhale. The first breath practice taught and the foundation for the rest.

title: Victorious Breath
desc: A soft constriction at the glottis giving the breath an audible ocean quality. The default breath of vinyasa practice.

title: Alternate Nostril Breath
desc: Breathing through one nostril at a time in a fixed cycle. The most widely prescribed balancing pranayama and the safest to self-practise.

title: Skull-Shining Breath
desc: Rapid forceful exhalations with passive inhalations. Classically a cleansing kriya rather than a pranayama, and strongly heating.

title: Bellows Breath
desc: Forceful inhalation and exhalation in equal measure. The most heating breath practice in the repertoire and not for beginners.

title: Cooling Breath
desc: Inhaling through a rolled tongue. Explicitly cooling, and the classical answer to excess pitta or summer heat.

title: Hissing Breath
desc: Inhaling through clenched teeth with a hiss. The alternative to sitali for those who cannot roll the tongue.

title: Humming Bee Breath
desc: A soft humming on every exhale with the ears closed. Reliably calming and one of the few practices with reasonable modern evidence for anxiety.

title: Victorious Breath with Retention
desc: Ujjayi with deliberate breath retention after inhale or exhale. Retention is where pranayama becomes genuinely risky without a teacher.

title: Equal Breath
desc: Inhale and exhale matched to the same count. The simplest way to steady an agitated breath and the entry to all ratio work.

title: Extended Exhale
desc: Lengthening the exhale to roughly twice the inhale. The most direct breath lever on the parasympathetic system.

title: Ocean Breath Seated
desc: Ujjayi practised seated and still rather than during movement. Where the quality of the breath can actually be examined.

title: Root Lock
desc: A lift of the pelvic floor held subtly through practice. The most talked-about and least accurately taught of the three locks.

title: Abdominal Lock
desc: Drawing the abdomen up and back under the ribs on an empty breath. Strongly stimulating to the digestive fire and never done on a full stomach.

title: Throat Lock
desc: The chin drawing toward the sternum during retention. Protects the head and heart from the pressure that retention creates.

title: Great Lock
desc: All three locks applied together. The classical culmination of bandha practice and appropriate only with an established foundation.

title: Consciousness Gesture
desc: Index finger and thumb touching, palms down on the knees. The most common seated hand gesture, said to turn awareness inward.

title: Knowledge Gesture
desc: Index finger and thumb touching with palms turned up. The receptive counterpart to chin mudra.

title: Life Gesture
desc: Ring and little finger meeting the thumb. Traditionally associated with vitality and used in longer seated practice.

title: Vital Air Gesture
desc: Middle and ring fingers to the thumb, associated with the downward-moving breath and elimination.

title: Great Gesture
desc: A seated forward hold combining all three locks with retention. One of the oldest practices named in the hatha texts.

title: Stomach Churning
desc: Isolating and rolling the abdominal recti on an empty breath. The most difficult kriya to learn and among the most strongly claimed for digestion.

title: Alternating Nostril Cleansing
desc: Alternate nostril breathing extended with counted ratios and retention. The bridge between simple breathing and formal pranayama.

title: Eye Cleansing Gaze
desc: Steady unblinking gaze at a candle flame until the eyes water, then holding the afterimage. A concentration practice classed among the cleansing kriyas.

title: Seated Meditation
desc: Sustained undirected awareness in a stable seat. The seventh limb, and the destination the physical practice is arranged to serve.

title: Concentration Practice
desc: Holding attention on a single object. The sixth limb, and the discipline that makes dhyana possible.

title: Sense Withdrawal
desc: Deliberately withdrawing attention from sensory input. The fifth limb and the hinge between the outer and inner practices.

title: Yogic Sleep
desc: A guided rotation of awareness through the body while lying completely still. Deeply restorative and the most accessible entry to formal meditation.

title: Body Scan
desc: A shortened rotation of consciousness through the body. Suitable at the end of any practice in place of a longer savasana.

title: Mantra Repetition
desc: Silent or whispered repetition of a mantra, often counted on a mala. The most widely practised meditation technique in the tradition.

title: Sun Salutation A
desc: The nine-movement salutation cycle linking fold, plank, chaturanga, upward dog and downward dog. The engine of every vinyasa practice.

title: Sun Salutation B
desc: The longer salutation adding chair pose and warrior I to each round. Substantially more heating than the A form.

title: Classical Sun Salutation
desc: The twelve-position hatha salutation using knees-chest-chin and cobra rather than chaturanga and upward dog. Gentler on the shoulders.

title: Moon Salutation
desc: A lateral, cooling counterpart to the sun salutation moving through goddess, triangle and side lunges. Modern in origin and explicitly pitta-pacifying.

title: Half Sun Salutation
desc: The standing half of the salutation — fold, half lift, rise — without the floor sequence. The standard warm-up opening.

title: Warrior I at Wall
desc: Warrior I with the back heel against a wall so the alignment can be felt rather than guessed.

title: Warrior II with Block
desc: Warrior II with a block under the front thigh to build endurance without collapsing.

title: Triangle with Block
desc: Triangle with the lower hand on a block so the chest can stay open rather than rotating down.

title: Bound Extended Side Angle
desc: Side angle with the arms binding beneath the front thigh. Adds a deep shoulder opening to an already strong leg shape.

title: Bound Triangle
desc: Triangle with a bind wrapping behind the back. Requires the shoulders to open before the pose can be entered at all.

title: Warrior II to Reverse Flow
desc: Cycling between warrior II, reverse warrior and side angle. The standard standing flow of a level-one class.

title: Skandasana
desc: A deep side lunge with one leg straight and the other bent to a squat. Opens the adductors under load.

title: Side Lunge
desc: A wide lateral lunge with the torso upright. The gentler precursor to skandasana.

title: Runner's Lunge
desc: A lunge with both hands framing the front foot and the back leg long. The most common transitional shape in vinyasa.

title: Half Split
desc: Front leg straight and hips stacked back over the rear knee. The honest preparation for full splits.

title: Full Split
desc: The front-to-back split named for Hanuman's leap. Years of consistent work for most bodies and never to be forced.

title: Middle Split
desc: The side-to-side split with the legs in one straight line. Depends almost entirely on adductor length.

title: Monkey Pose Prep with Blocks
desc: Splits approached with blocks under the hips so the pelvis stays square. The version that actually builds range.

title: Pyramid with Blocks
desc: Pyramid pose with hands on blocks so the spine can lengthen instead of rounding.

title: Standing Forward Fold with Clasp
desc: A forward fold with the hands clasped behind and the arms falling overhead. Combines hamstring and shoulder opening.

title: Rag Doll
desc: A forward fold with soft knees and the head hanging heavy. Releases the neck and low back without any hamstring demand.

title: Bound Ardha Chandrasana
desc: Half moon with the top foot caught behind in a sugarcane bind. Balance and a quadriceps stretch at once.

title: Sugarcane Pose
desc: Half moon with the top leg bent and caught, opening into a backbend. Modern in name and demanding in practice.

title: Tree with Hands Overhead
desc: Tree pose with the arms extending overhead rather than at the heart. Raises the centre of gravity and the difficulty.

title: Toe Stand
desc: Balancing on the ball of one foot in a half lotus squat. Extremely demanding on the ankle and knee.

title: Chair Pose on Toes
desc: Chair pose with the heels lifted. Adds a strong calf and balance demand to an already heating shape.

title: Revolved Hand-to-Big-Toe
desc: Extended hand-to-toe with the torso rotating away. Balance without a visual reference on a straight leg.

title: Eagle Arms Only
desc: The double arm wrap of eagle taken seated. Opens the rear shoulder and upper back with no balance demand.

title: Cow Face Arms Only
desc: The overhead-and-behind clasp of cow face without the leg position. The most useful shoulder opener for desk-bound bodies.

title: Reverse Prayer
desc: Palms pressed together behind the back between the shoulder blades. Demands wrist and shoulder range most people lack.

title: Shoulder Flossing with Strap
desc: Taking a strap in wide hands from front to back overhead. The safest way to restore shoulder range.

title: Neck Rolls
desc: Slow circles and half circles of the head. Releases the cervical tension that undermines every seated practice.

title: Wrist Circles
desc: Circling and flexing the wrists. Essential preparation before any weight-bearing on the hands.

title: Ankle Rotations
desc: Rotating the ankles in both directions. The first movement in the classical pawanmuktasana joint series.

title: Butterfly Flaps
desc: Bound angle with the knees moving up and down. Warms the hips before any deeper opening.

title: Seated Neck Stretch
desc: Ear drawing toward the shoulder with the opposite hand anchoring. Directly targets the upper trapezius.

title: Reclined Figure Four Twist
desc: Reclined pigeon taken across the body into a twist. Releases the outer hip and low back together.

title: Reclined Big Toe Side
desc: Supine hand-to-toe with the leg opening out to the side. Adductor length without any balance demand.

title: Reclined Twist with Extended Leg
desc: Legs extended and swept to one side while the shoulders stay down. Stronger on the obliques than the knees-bent version.

title: Bridge with Block Between Thighs
desc: Bridge with a block squeezed between the thighs so the adductors and glutes engage together.

title: One-Legged Bridge
desc: Bridge with one leg extended. Doubles the load on the standing glute and exposes side-to-side imbalance.

title: One-Legged Wheel
desc: Wheel with one leg lifted. Among the most demanding backbends and dependent on an already stable full wheel.

title: Bow with Strap
desc: Bow approached with a strap around the ankles. Lets the chest open before the shoulders can reach.

title: Half Frog
desc: Prone with one foot pressed toward the hip. A quadriceps and hip flexor opener with a mild chest lift.

title: Cobra with Hands Lifted
desc: Cobra held with the hands hovering off the floor. Proves the lift is coming from the back and not the arms.

title: Superman
desc: Prone with arms and legs lifting simultaneously and reaching long. Pure posterior chain conditioning.

title: Swimming Locust
desc: Locust with the arms and legs alternating like a swimmer. Builds endurance in the low back without a long static hold.

title: Camel with Hands on Sacrum
desc: Camel with the hands supporting the low back rather than reaching for the heels. The right entry for almost everyone.

title: Camel on Blocks
desc: Camel with blocks beside the ankles to shorten the reach. Lets the chest open before the spine has to.

title: Dolphin to Forearm Stand Drill
desc: Dolphin with alternating leg lifts against a wall. The safe drill for building forearm stand.

title: Shoulderstand at Wall
desc: Shoulderstand with the feet against a wall to control the load on the neck. How the pose should be learned.

title: Supported Shoulderstand with Blankets
desc: Shoulderstand with folded blankets under the shoulders so the cervical curve is preserved. The Iyengar standard, and the only version many teachers will now teach.

title: Legs Up Wall with Bolster
desc: Legs up the wall with a bolster raising the pelvis. Deepens the mild inversion while remaining entirely passive.

title: Supported Child's Pose
desc: Child's pose over a bolster so the torso is fully carried. Suitable for very long holds and for pregnancy with the knees wide.

title: Side-Lying Savasana
desc: Final rest taken on the side with support between the knees. The recommended form in pregnancy and for anyone uncomfortable on the back.

title: Supported Forward Fold
desc: A seated fold resting the torso entirely on a bolster. Quiet and long rather than deep.

title: Reclined Butterfly with Blocks
desc: Reclined bound angle with blocks under the thighs so the groin can release without strain.

title: Melting Heart
desc: Hips high, chest and chin melting toward the floor. A yin shape held for minutes rather than breaths.

title: Dragon Pose
desc: The yin form of a deep lunge held for several minutes. Targets connective tissue rather than muscle.

title: Sleeping Swan
desc: The yin form of pigeon, held long and unforced with the torso folding down.

title: Caterpillar
desc: A rounded seated fold held for minutes with no attempt to straighten the spine. Deliberately targets the fascia of the back line.

title: Shoelace Pose
desc: The yin version of cow face legs, held long. One of the most effective outer hip releases available.

title: Saddle Pose
desc: Reclining back from kneeling and held for minutes. Very strong on the knees and to be approached with real caution.

title: Banana Pose
desc: Lying on the back curved into a crescent. A long passive stretch of the whole side body and the intercostals.

title: Square Pose
desc: Firelog held in the yin manner for several minutes. Intense and slow rather than muscular.

title: Snail Pose
desc: The yin form of plough with a rounded spine held long. Considerable load on the cervical spine and not for beginners.

title: Deer Pose
desc: A seated shape with one hip internally and one externally rotated. Works both rotations of the hip at once.

title: Sphinx Yin Hold
desc: Sphinx held for several minutes so the lumbar spine compresses gradually. The gentlest of the yin backbends.

title: Chair Mountain
desc: Seated tall at the front of a chair with the feet grounded. The reference posture for the whole chair sequence.

title: Chair Forward Fold
desc: Folding forward over the thighs from a seated position. Accessible when standing folds are not.

title: Chair Warrior
desc: A warrior shape built around a chair with one leg extended back. Keeps the leg work available for limited mobility.

title: Chair Eagle Arms
desc: The eagle arm wrap performed sitting. Opens the upper back with no balance requirement.

title: Chair Pigeon
desc: Ankle crossed over the opposite knee while seated. The figure-four hip opener for chairs and desks.

title: Chair Cat-Cow
desc: Spinal flexion and extension in a chair. The most useful movement for anyone sitting all day.

title: Chair Twist
desc: A gentle seated rotation using the chair back for leverage. Safe for almost every body.

title: Wall Downward Dog
desc: Hands on a wall with the torso folding to horizontal. Teaches the shape without any weight on the wrists.

title: Wall Tree
desc: Tree pose with the back against a wall. Removes the fear of falling so alignment can be learned.

title: Wall Chair
desc: Chair pose with the back sliding down a wall. Isolates the quadriceps without demanding balance.

title: Wall Bridge
desc: Bridge with the feet pressing a wall so the glutes can find the lift without gripping the low back.

title: Prenatal Wide Squat
desc: A supported wide squat used through pregnancy to open the pelvis. Held with support rather than depth.

title: Prenatal Cat-Cow
desc: Cat-cow on all fours during pregnancy, favouring the neutral and cow phases. Relieves lumbar load.

title: Prenatal Side-Lying Rest
desc: Left-side-lying rest with support between the knees. The recommended final rest after the first trimester.

title: Prenatal Supported Goddess
desc: A wide-legged bend supported at a wall or chair. Builds leg endurance for labour without balance risk.

title: Standing Pelvic Tilts
desc: Small forward and back tilts of the pelvis standing. The simplest way to find lumbar movement.

title: Standing Twist
desc: Loose rotational swinging of the torso with the arms trailing. A classical warm-up from the pawanmuktasana series.

title: Shoulder Shrugs
desc: Lifting and releasing the shoulders with the breath. Releases the trapezius before any overhead work.

title: Arm Circles
desc: Full circles of the arms in both directions. Warms the shoulder joint through its whole range.

title: Hip Circles
desc: Circling the pelvis in both directions with the feet planted. Mobilises the hip before deeper opening.

title: Knee Circles
desc: Gentle circling of the knees with the hands resting on them. From the classical joint-freeing series.

title: Squat and Rise
desc: Repeated lowering and rising from a squat with the breath. Builds heat quickly and is strongly kapha-reducing.

title: Standing Knee Hug
desc: Standing on one leg with the other knee drawn into the chest. Balance and hip flexion together.

title: Standing Quad Stretch
desc: Catching one foot behind while standing. The preparation for dancer pose and a direct quadriceps stretch.

title: Standing Figure Four
desc: A one-legged chair pose with the other ankle crossed over the knee. Opens the outer hip under load.

title: Crescent with Blocks
desc: High lunge with hands on blocks either side. Stabilises the shape while the legs build endurance.

title: Warrior III at Wall
desc: Warrior III with the hands pressing a wall. The right way to build the strength before removing support.

title: Downward Dog with Blocks
desc: Downward dog with hands elevated on blocks. Reduces the wrist angle for anyone with wrist pain.

title: Puppy at Chair
desc: Forearms on a chair seat with the chest melting down. A shoulder opener that needs no floor work.

title: Standing Wide Fold with Blocks
desc: The wide fold with hands on blocks so the spine stays long. The version that actually builds range.

title: Cobra at Wall
desc: A standing chest opener with hands on a wall. Teaches the thoracic extension of cobra without the floor.

title: Seated Meditation on Chair
desc: Meditation seated in a chair with the feet flat and spine free of the backrest. The stable seat for most modern practitioners.

title: Walking Meditation
desc: Slow deliberate walking with attention on each footfall. The classical alternative when sitting is not possible.

title: Alternate Leg Raises
desc: Single leg raises from lying with the low back pressed down. From the pawanmuktasana series and the safest core entry.

title: Double Leg Raises
desc: Both legs raising and lowering together. Twice the lumbar load of single raises and often attempted too early.

title: Cycling Legs
desc: Pedalling the legs in the air on the back. Simple hip flexor and abdominal conditioning.

title: Rocking Boat
desc: Rolling forward and back on the spine from a boat shape. Massages the back while conditioning the core.

title: Churning the Mill
desc: Seated with legs wide, hands clasped, circling the torso as if turning a millstone. A classical abdominal and waist practice.

title: Boat Rowing
desc: Seated rowing motion with the legs extended. Warms the whole trunk in the pawanmuktasana sequence.

title: Wood Chopping
desc: A squatting chopping motion with clasped hands. Heating, dynamic and strongly kapha-reducing.

title: Crow Walking
desc: Walking forward in a deep squat. Classically prescribed for digestion and among the most heating of the simple practices.

title: Dynamic Spinal Twist
desc: Seated with legs extended, twisting side to side to reach the opposite foot. A warming spinal rotation.

title: Standing Forward Bend Dynamic
desc: Repeatedly folding and rising with the breath. Warms the hamstrings before any static hold.

title: Sun Salutation with Lunges
desc: A salutation variant stepping into low lunges rather than jumping. Lower impact and better for stiff bodies.

title: Sun Salutation C
desc: A gentler salutation using low lunge and cobra throughout. Common in hatha and beginner classes.

title: Kneeling Sun Salutation
desc: The salutation cycle performed entirely from the knees. Accessible for limited standing tolerance.

title: Seated Sun Salutation
desc: The salutation shapes adapted to a chair. Keeps the breath-movement link available to anyone.

title: Camel to Child Flow
desc: Alternating between camel and child's pose. Backbend and counterpose in one breath cycle.

title: Cat-Cow to Downward Dog Flow
desc: Moving between tabletop, cat-cow and downward dog. The standard opening flow of most classes.

title: Lunge to Half Split Flow
desc: Rocking between a low lunge and a half split. Works hip flexors and hamstrings alternately.

title: Warrior II to Half Moon Flow
desc: Cycling between warrior II and half moon. Trains the balance transition rather than the static shape.

title: Scorpion Pose
desc: Forearm stand with the spine arching and the feet reaching toward the head. Inversion and deep backbend at once.

title: Handstand Scorpion
desc: Handstand with the spine arching into a scorpion shape. Among the most advanced postures practised.

title: Feathered Peacock
desc: Forearm stand entered with the hands clasped. More stable at the base and harder to press up into.

title: Lotus Headstand
desc: Headstand with the legs folding into lotus. Requires both a solid headstand and a comfortable lotus.

title: Lotus Shoulderstand
desc: Shoulderstand with the legs in lotus and the knees pressing into the hands.

title: Embryo in Womb
desc: From shoulderstand, the lotus legs folding down toward the chest. A deeply compressed closing shape.

title: Yogic Sleep Pose
desc: Lying on the back with both legs behind the head and the hands bound. One of the deepest hip and hamstring shapes in the tradition.

title: One Leg Behind Head
desc: One leg hooked behind the head while seated. External rotation and hamstring length taken to their limit.

title: Both Legs Behind Head
desc: Both legs crossed behind the head while balanced on the sitting bones.

title: Formidable Face Pose
desc: Chest and chin grounded with the legs lifting and arching overhead.

title: Destroyer of the Universe
desc: A side arm balance with one leg behind the head. Balance, rotation and extreme hip range together.

title: Sundial Pose
desc: Seated with one leg lifted over the shoulder and extended while the torso opens.

title: Elephant Trunk Pose
desc: One leg hooked over the upper arm with the body lifting on the hands.

title: Two-Footed Arm Balance
desc: Both legs hooked over the upper arms with the feet crossed. The compressed precursor to firefly.

title: Sage Koundinya I
desc: A twisted arm balance with the legs extended in opposite directions.

title: Sage Koundinya II
desc: An open-legged arm balance with one leg forward over the arm and one extended back.

title: Split Arm Balance
desc: Crow with one leg extending straight back. Requires real core control to avoid collapsing forward.

title: Peacock Feather Pose
desc: Peacock pose with the legs in lotus. Adds the knee demand of lotus to an already extreme wrist load.

title: Sideways Crow
desc: Side crow with the legs extending straight rather than stacked.

title: Rooster in Lotus
desc: Arms threaded through a lotus and the whole body rocking or balancing. From the Ashtanga primary series.

title: Frog in Lotus Roll
desc: Rolling in a circle while bound in the embryo shape. Traditionally nine rolls to complete a circle.

title: Noose Pose
desc: A deep squat with the arms binding around the legs in a twist. Demands ankle range before rotation is even possible.

title: Sage Twist with Bind
desc: A bound seated twist with one leg in half lotus. The most demanding of the four Marichi poses.

title: Sage Marichi II
desc: A bound forward fold with one leg in half lotus.

title: Reverse Table with Head Back
desc: Tabletop with the head releasing back and the chest lifting high.

title: Bridge with Clasp
desc: Bridge with the hands clasped beneath the body and the shoulders rolling under.

title: Wheel from Standing
desc: Dropping back into wheel from standing and coming up again. The most demanding backbend transition.

title: Pigeon with Bind
desc: King pigeon with both hands catching the back foot overhead.

title: Full Pigeon
desc: Kneeling and arching all the way back until the hands reach the feet. Among the deepest backbends in the tradition.

title: Cobra Full Expression
desc: Cobra taken to full depth with the feet reaching toward the head.

title: Bow with Feet to Head
desc: Bow pose taken until the feet touch the crown.

title: Side Bow
desc: Bow pose rolled to one side. Adds a lateral element and a deeper shoulder stretch.

title: Standing Split with Bind
desc: Standing split with a hand catching the standing ankle.

title: Grasshopper Variation
desc: A twisted arm balance with one foot hooked across the opposite arm and the other leg extended.

title: Hurdler Pose
desc: An arm balance with one leg forward and straight and the other back, like a hurdler mid-stride.

title: Crow with Head Down
desc: Crow lowering the crown lightly to the floor as preparation for tripod headstand.

title: Wall Handstand Hold
desc: Handstand held with the heels resting on a wall. Where the strength and alignment are actually built.

title: Chest-to-Wall Handstand
desc: Handstand facing the wall so the body must find true vertical rather than banana back.

title: Headstand Leg Variations
desc: Headstand with the legs moving into splits, wide angle or lotus. Only appropriate once the base is unshakeable.

title: Shoulderstand Leg Variations
desc: Shoulderstand with the legs moving into splits, wide angle or lotus.

title: Bound Lotus
desc: Full lotus with the arms crossing behind to catch the opposite toes.

title: Fish in Lotus
desc: Fish pose with the legs bound in lotus. The classical full expression of the pose.

title: Downward Dog with Twist
desc: Downward dog with one hand crossing to catch the opposite ankle.

title: Revolved Lunge with Bind
desc: A revolved low lunge with the arms binding beneath the front thigh.

title: Revolved Side Angle with Bind
desc: Revolved side angle with a full bind. Rotation, leg endurance and shoulder opening at once.

title: Half Bound Standing Forward Fold
desc: Standing on one leg in half lotus with the foot bound and the torso folding forward.

title: Sleeping Vishnu
desc: Side-lying with the top leg lifted and held at the toe. Named for Vishnu reclining on the cosmic serpent.

title: Side-Lying Leg Lifts
desc: Side-lying leg raises. Simple conditioning for the outer hip and lateral trunk.

title: Reclined Cow Face
desc: Cow face legs taken lying down. Removes the spinal load while keeping the hip opening.

title: Corpse with Bolster
desc: Final rest with a bolster under the knees and support under the head. The version most low backs actually need.

title: Guided Relaxation
desc: Final rest guided by voice through progressive release. The bridge between savasana and yoga nidra.

title: Standing Deep Breathing
desc: The opening breath of the Bikram series, standing with fingers interlaced under the chin.

title: Half Moon with Hands to Feet
desc: The Bikram half moon, a standing side bend and back bend followed by a full forward fold.

title: Awkward Pose
desc: The three-part Bikram chair sequence: arms forward, heels lifted, then sinking low with knees together.

title: Standing Bow Pulling
desc: The Bikram standing bow, kicking one foot back and up while the opposite arm reaches forward.

title: Balancing Stick
desc: A single-leg T shape with arms and lifted leg forming one horizontal line, held briefly and intensely.

title: Standing Separate Leg Stretching
desc: A wide-legged forward fold from the Bikram series with the crown reaching toward the floor.

title: Standing Separate Leg Head to Knee
desc: A compressed fold over one straight leg with the chin tucked, from the Bikram series.

title: Tree Pose Bikram
desc: The Bikram tree with the foot drawn high into half lotus against the standing thigh.

title: Wind Removing Pose
desc: Single and double knee compression into the abdomen, worked one side at a time then together.

title: Fixed Firm Pose
desc: Kneeling and reclining fully back onto the floor with the knees together. Extremely demanding on the knee.

title: Rabbit Pose
desc: Kneeling and rolling onto the crown with the heels held, creating deep spinal flexion.

title: Spine Twisting Pose
desc: The closing twist of the Bikram series, taken with a specific hand and knee placement.

title: Blowing in Firm
desc: Kapalabhati performed kneeling, the closing practice of the Bikram sequence.

title: Eagle Bikram
desc: The Bikram eagle, sinking deeper in the legs than the vinyasa version usually asks.

title: Padangusthasana Big Toe Pose
desc: A standing fold gripping the big toes, the first standing pose of the Ashtanga primary series.

title: Padahastasana Hand Under Foot
desc: A standing fold with the palms slid beneath the soles of the feet.

title: Utthita Trikonasana A
desc: The Ashtanga triangle with the hand gripping the big toe rather than resting on the shin.

title: Utthita Trikonasana B
desc: The revolved triangle of the Ashtanga sequence, entered from a specific foot alignment.

title: Prasarita Padottanasana A
desc: The first of the four Ashtanga wide-legged folds, hands on the floor between the feet.

title: Prasarita Padottanasana B
desc: The wide fold with the hands on the hips, demanding more from the core to descend.

title: Prasarita Padottanasana D
desc: The wide fold with the big toes gripped, the deepest of the four.

title: Utthita Parsvasahita
desc: The extended hand-to-toe balance with the leg opened out to the side.

title: Ardha Baddha Padmottanasana Ashtanga
desc: Standing half lotus with a bind behind the back and a fold over the standing leg.

title: Utkatasana Ashtanga
desc: The Ashtanga chair pose entered from a jump and held for five breaths.

title: Virabhadrasana A and B Flow
desc: The paired warrior sequence of the Ashtanga series moving directly from the first to the second.

title: Purvottanasana Ashtanga
desc: The upward plank counterpose that follows every seated forward bend in the primary series.

title: Triang Mukha Eka Pada Paschimottanasana
desc: A seated fold with one leg folded back in hero position and the other extended.

title: Janu Sirsasana B
desc: Head-to-knee with the folded foot placed beneath the perineum and the body sitting on the heel.

title: Janu Sirsasana C
desc: Head-to-knee with the folded foot on its toes at a sharp angle. The most demanding of the three on the ankle.

title: Navasana Ashtanga Five Rounds
desc: Five boat holds separated by lifts, the conditioning set of the Ashtanga primary series.

title: Baddha Konasana A and B
desc: Bound angle held upright and then folded forward with the chin reaching the floor.

title: Upavistha Konasana A and B
desc: The wide-angle fold followed by a balance lifting both legs off the floor.

title: Supta Konasana
desc: Plough with the legs wide and the big toes gripped, then rolling up to a seated fold.

title: Ubhaya Padangusthasana
desc: A balance on the sitting bones with both legs straight up and the toes held.

title: Urdhva Mukha Paschimottanasana
desc: Balanced on the sitting bones with the legs straight up and drawn toward the face.

title: Setu Bandhasana Ashtanga
desc: A bridge lifted onto the crown of the head with the feet turned out. Very strong on the cervical spine.

title: Salamba Sarvangasana Ashtanga
desc: The closing shoulderstand of the Ashtanga sequence, held long before plough and ear pressure.

title: Uttana Padasana
desc: Fish pose with the legs and arms lifted at an angle. A demanding chest opener and core hold at once.

title: Baddha Hasta Sirsasana
desc: Headstand with the forearms crossed rather than the fingers interlaced.

title: Mukta Hasta Sirsasana
desc: Headstand with the arms free and palms flat, offering far less base than the bound version.

title: Yoga Mudra in Lotus
desc: Lotus with the arms bound behind and the torso folding forward to the floor.

title: Tolasana Lift
desc: The closing lift of the Ashtanga sequence, held for twenty-five breaths in the traditional count.

title: Pranidhanasana
desc: A kneeling surrender pose with the forehead down and arms extended forward, held in stillness.

title: Ananda Balasana Rock
desc: Happy baby with a gentle side-to-side rocking that massages the lumbar spine.

title: Supta Tadasana
desc: Lying flat with the arms overhead and the whole body lengthening in two directions.

title: Makarasana Crocodile
desc: Lying prone with the forehead on stacked forearms. The classical prone rest between backbends.

title: Advasana
desc: Face-down rest with the arms extended forward. Prescribed traditionally for a strained low back.

title: Jyestikasana
desc: Prone rest with the hands clasped behind the neck and the elbows down.

title: Matsya Kridasana
desc: The flapping fish pose, prone with one knee drawn up to the side. Traditionally recommended for sleep and digestion.

title: Shashankasana
desc: The moon or hare pose, kneeling and folding forward with the arms extended.

title: Shashank Bhujangasana
desc: A dynamic movement sliding from the hare pose forward into cobra and back.

title: Marjari Asana Dynamic
desc: The classical Bihar School cat sequence, moving the spine through flexion and extension with a set breath rhythm.

title: Vyaghrasana Tiger
desc: The tiger pose, arching and rounding on all fours while one leg extends and draws in.

title: Ushtrasana Dynamic
desc: Moving in and out of camel with the breath rather than holding the arch.

title: Kandharasana
desc: The shoulder pose, a bridge entered by gripping the ankles with the feet close to the buttocks.

title: Grivasana Neck Pose
desc: A supported neck arch with the crown grounded and the shoulders lifted. To be entered very slowly.

title: Naukasana Prone Boat
desc: The prone boat, lifting arms, chest and legs together into a shallow curve.

title: Setu Asana
desc: The bridge pose of the Bihar School, entered from a seated position with straight legs and arms.

title: Gomukhasana Dynamic
desc: Moving in and out of the cow face arm bind with the breath rather than holding it.

title: Vatayanasana Horse Face
desc: A half lotus kneeling balance with the arms in eagle. Very demanding on the knee and the hip.

title: Durvasasana
desc: Standing on one leg with the other hooked behind the head. Among the hardest standing balances in the tradition.

title: Ruchikasana
desc: A standing forward fold with one leg behind the head. The folded counterpart to Durvasasana.

title: Skandasana Standing
desc: Standing upright with one leg behind the head, hands at the heart. A rarely achieved shape.

title: Viranchyasana
desc: A seated shape with one leg behind the head and the torso folding over the other.

title: Chakorasana
desc: An arm balance with one leg behind the head and the other extended straight up.

title: Bhairavasana
desc: Reclined with one leg cradled behind the head and the hands at the heart.

title: Supta Trivikramasana
desc: Reclined with one leg drawn out to the side and down toward the floor beside the head.

title: Trivikramasana
desc: A standing split held vertically with one leg raised straight up beside the ear.

title: Natarajasana Full
desc: The full dancer with both hands catching the raised foot overhead and the spine deeply arched.

title: Padangustha Dhanurasana
desc: Bow pose with the feet caught overhead by the big toes and drawn toward the head.

title: Rajakapotasana Full
desc: The full king pigeon on both knees with the head reaching the feet.

title: Tiriang Mukhottanasana
desc: A standing backbend descending until the hands catch the ankles. Among the deepest spinal extensions practised.

title: Viparita Chakrasana
desc: Tipping over from wheel into a standing position, or the reverse. A dynamic backbend transition.

title: Vrschikasana II
desc: Scorpion entered from handstand rather than forearm stand, with straight arms throughout.

title: Sayanasana
desc: A forearm balance with the legs in lotus folded toward the head.

title: Bhujangasana Full
desc: The full cobra with the arms straight, the head reaching back and the feet approaching the crown.

title: Kapotasana Full
desc: The full pigeon backbend with the forearms on the floor and the head at the feet.

title: Eka Pada Viparita Dandasana
desc: An inverted staff backbend on the forearms with one leg lifted to vertical.

title: Dwi Pada Viparita Dandasana
desc: The inverted staff pose, a deep backbend supported on the forearms and the crown.

title: Mandalasana
desc: Walking the legs in a full circle around the head while inverted in a backbend.

title: Flip Dog
desc: Flipping from downward dog through side plank into a one-handed backbend. Entirely modern and popular in flow classes.

title: Fallen Triangle
desc: From plank, one leg sweeping beneath the body and extending while the opposite hand lifts. A modern transitional shape.

title: Rock Star
desc: A dynamic lift from wild thing with both feet leaving the floor briefly. Modern, athletic and rarely taught outside flow studios.

title: Puppy Dog Twist
desc: Extended puppy with one arm threading beneath the body into a thoracic rotation.

title: Waterfall
desc: A supported shoulderstand variant with the legs floating rather than fully vertical.

title: Plow to Shoulderstand Flow
desc: Moving between plough and shoulderstand with control rather than momentum.

title: Bound Half Moon
desc: Half moon with a bind wrapping the standing thigh.

title: Bird of Paradise
desc: Standing from a bound side angle and extending the bound leg straight. Modern in name and demanding on hamstring and balance together.

title: Bound Extended Side Angle to Bird
desc: The transition from a bound side angle up into bird of paradise, practised as one movement.

title: Cactus Arms Backbend
desc: A standing chest opener with the arms bent at ninety degrees and the elbows drawing back.

title: Heart Bench
desc: Reclining lengthways over a bolster so the thoracic spine opens passively. A modern restorative staple.

title: Supported Half Frog
desc: Half frog supported on a bolster so the quadriceps releases without a knee demand.

title: Legs on Chair
desc: Lying with the calves resting on a chair seat. The gentlest way to unload the lumbar spine.

title: Supported Twist over Bolster
desc: A long passive twist with the knees resting on a bolster to one side.

title: Side-Lying Quad Stretch
desc: Lying on one side and catching the top foot behind. A safe quadriceps stretch with no balance demand.

title: Thread the Needle Supine
desc: The supine figure-four with the hands drawing the underneath thigh toward the chest.

title: Windshield Wipers
desc: Knees falling slowly side to side with the feet planted. The gentlest possible spinal rotation.

title: Bridge Rolls
desc: Rolling the spine up and down from a bridge one vertebra at a time.

title: Cat Pulling Its Tail
desc: A long yin twist catching the top foot behind while the legs scissor. Combines rotation with a quadriceps stretch.

title: Swan Dive
desc: A long-held standing fold with soft knees, targeting fascia rather than muscle.

title: Toe Squat
desc: Kneeling on tucked toes. Extremely intense on the plantar fascia and held for minutes in yin practice.

title: Ankle Stretch
desc: Kneeling with the tops of the feet flat and the knees lifted. The counterpose to the toe squat.

title: Half Butterfly
desc: A yin fold over one straight leg held several minutes with a rounded spine.

title: Reclining Twist Yin
desc: A supine twist held five minutes per side. The standard closing shape of a yin practice.

title: Straddle Yin
desc: The wide-angle seated fold held for minutes at a time with full support if needed.

title: Bananasana Side
desc: The banana curve held long on each side, targeting the fascial line from armpit to hip.

title: Supported Fish Yin
desc: A long passive chest opening over a block or bolster placed under the thoracic spine.

title: Iyengar Wall Rope Dog
desc: Downward dog with the hips supported in wall ropes so the spine can traction. Distinctly Iyengar.

title: Chair Shoulderstand
desc: Shoulderstand fully supported on a chair with the shoulders on a bolster. The Iyengar restorative inversion.

title: Supported Backbend over Bolster
desc: A long passive backbend over a bolster or backbender. Opens the thoracic spine without any effort.

title: Wall Splits
desc: Legs wide against a wall while lying on the back, gravity doing the work over several minutes.

title: Belted Shoulderstand
desc: Shoulderstand with a belt around the upper arms to hold the shoulder position. An Iyengar solution to collapsing elbows.

title: Block Between Blocks Bridge
desc: A supported bridge with blocks under both the sacrum and the shoulders.

title: Prone Savasana
desc: Final rest taken face down. Often more settling than the supine version for an anxious nervous system.

title: Frog at Wall
desc: The frog shape with the feet against a wall so the depth can be controlled precisely.

title: Ego Eradicator
desc: Arms at sixty degrees with breath of fire, from the Kundalini repertoire. Strongly heating and named for its intent.

title: Breath of Fire
desc: A rapid even-paced diaphragmatic breath from the Kundalini tradition, distinct from kapalabhati in rhythm.

title: Sat Kriya
desc: Kneeling with arms overhead, pulling the navel in rhythm with a chanted mantra. The central Kundalini kriya.

title: Spinal Flex
desc: Rapid seated spinal flexion and extension holding the ankles, used to warm the spine in Kundalini practice.

title: Life Nerve Stretch
desc: A dynamic seated fold pulsing with the breath rather than held static.

title: Archer Pose
desc: A lunge with the arms drawn as if pulling a bow, held long. Builds determination as much as leg endurance.

title: Frog Squats
desc: Repeated deep squats on the toes with the heels together. One of the most strongly heating practices in the Kundalini set.

title: Stretch Pose
desc: Lying with heels and shoulders six inches off the floor with breath of fire. The Kundalini navel-strengthening hold.

title: Chair Twist Kundalini
desc: Seated with hands on the shoulders, twisting rhythmically side to side with the breath.

title: Yoga Squat Hold
desc: The deep squat held for several minutes rather than seconds. Restores a range most adults have lost.

title: Wall Sit Yoga
desc: The wall-supported chair held for minutes. Pure quadriceps endurance and strongly kapha-reducing.

title: Standing Wide Fold Twist
desc: The wide-legged fold with one hand to the floor and the other reaching up in rotation.

title: Downward Dog Calf Stretch
desc: Pedalling the heels in downward dog to release each calf in turn.

title: Ragdoll Sway
desc: A forward fold with the torso swaying gently side to side to release the low back.

title: Neck Release in Fold
desc: A forward fold with slow head nods and shakes to release cervical tension.
